activity.title: Just presented Swarm to 2,500+ people at ClawCon Michigan at Crisler Arena. Swarm is a multi-agent self-healing system that finds viral short-form content. It won me a Mac Mini at the YC x BrowserUse hackathon. One of the biggest challenges with long-running multi-agent systems is context management. Passing everything through the orchestrator gets messy, and summarizing is costly and time-consuming. That's why I gave each sub-agent its own state. A set of variables storing each sub-agents' discoveries, current task, search terms, and energy level. This lets the main orchestrator efficiently keep track of all of the sub-agents in real-time. Web-agents aren't quite there either. They stall, get stuck on captchas, and sometimes don't find anything valuable. That's where the energy level comes in. The energy level depletes over time, and gets reset on every new viral reel it finds. If a sub-agent's energy level gets to 0, then that sub-agent is redirected and copies the most successful sub-agents with a twist. For example, if a certain search term on TikTok is doing great, the failed sub-agent will attempt to try that same search term on YouTube shorts. This project goes past just marketing - The possibilities of long-running multi-agent systems like Swarm are endless and quite powerful. ClawCon Michigan was truly something special - I had a great time meeting everyone :) ...more

here's what I built for MHacks 2025 as a 2x high school hackathon winner ↓ I haven’t been sleeping much lately. Too many thoughts keeping me up. One of them has been hard to ignore: more than 5 billion people around the world still don’t have access to safe surgical care. That leads to about 18 million preventable deaths every year. That number hit me. I couldn’t stop thinking about what it would mean if someone I cared about was part of that statistic. In just 24 hours, I teamed up with Jacob Mazelin , Ethan Wang , and Yamato M. to build Surgent, a prototype for scalable surgical education. It uses Snap AR and a custom AI model powered by the Gemini API that can see, hear, and respond in real time. The AI gives suggestions and corrections as users go, helping future surgeons practice safely wherever they are. We built this to make surgical training more accessible to anyone, anywhere. Huge thanks to Peng Guo and Steven Le for supporting us on this project and the debugging sessions that made this product possible. Shout out to Alexander Salinas and Mihir Arya for making this event possible ...more

The Tech Roast Show ripped apart a project I poured 24 hours of heart, Gatorade (my “caffeine”), and sheer determination into. This past weekend, I attended MHacks 2025, my first hackathon as a university student. Walking in, I felt intimidated. Everyone looked like they had it all figured out. But then my team and I started talking about a problem too big to ignore: over 5 billion people worldwide still lack access to safe surgical care, leading to 18 million preventable deaths every year. That number shook me. I couldn’t stop thinking: What if someone I loved was part of that statistic? So, in just 24 hours, alongside Jacob Mazelin , Ethan Wang , and Yamato M. , we built Surgent, a prototype for scalable surgical education. Using Snap AR and a custom AI model that listens, sees, and suggests in real-time, we wanted to empower future surgeons, no matter where they live. Did it work perfectly? Not at all. Did we survive the roast? Barely, especially after the project was dubbed "Slop MD" by Jesse. But that’s the beauty of hackathons: you put yourself out there, fail in public, and leave a little braver (and a lot more sleep-deprived). Shoutout to my team for pushing through every “this will never work” momen, and to everyone at MHacks who reminded me why I love building in the first place. More on Surgent soon. ...more

Lotus Health was just named to the Forbes Next Billion-Dollar Startups 2026 list. I grew up translating doctor visits into Punjabi for my immigrant parents. At 18, I herniated two discs and learned firsthand how broken, confusing, and expensive American healthcare is when you don't have someone to guide you. That's why we built Lotus: 24/7 primary care powered by AI and real licensed physicians, available in 50+ languages. Our doctors can care for 10x the patients of a traditional practice. 60% of the companies on this list historically go on to become unicorns. Duolingo and DoorDash were on it once. But honestly, the number I care about most isn't the valuation. It's the number of people who get a doctor for the first time. Grateful to my team who show up every day like it's day one, our physicians, our patients, and our investors at CRV and Kleiner Perkins who believed early. We're just getting started on our vision of infinite care for all. Full list in the comments.

One sentence in, a finished comps workbook out. Deal work does not end in a chatbot answer or a half baked deliverable, it ends in a bullet proof deliverable that you can stand behind. This is the gap. Type the ask in plain English. The agent picks the peer set, pulls the filing data, calendarizes everyone to a common year end, and hands back an Excel workbook where every multiple is a live formula and every sourced figure carries its citation. Click any cell. Check the math. Check the source. Book a demo and we will run it on your own peer set.
